scope: Pinned core Model 1 numerical calculations and core survey table inference; raw-data extraction is covered by a separate data audit.

methods: Independent weighted Newton logistic estimates, separate periodontal and oral-health models
Independent PSU score totals and stratum-centered sandwich covariance, retaining all full-design PSUs for domain variance
Saved IRLS working-weight and working-residual variance convention verified against installed survey implementation
Coefficient, SE, residual-df t statistic, two-sided p value, OR and t-based 95% CI identities checked for every coefficient
Full-design construction followed by domain subset independently reconstructed and numerical cluster, strata, weights and degrees of freedom checked
Independent weighted means, category percentages and their design SEs from stratum/PSU influence totals
Independent ordinary Pearson statistic and fresh-design Rao-Scott F, degrees of freedom and p values
Independent Yes-minus-No mean-contrast survey t statistic, residual df and p values

design_findings.explanation: Four strata contain three PSUs. The design df is 152 minus 74, not an assumed two-PSU-per-stratum count. Both M1 models use the fixed primary domain and MEC two-year weight divided by five.

resolved_audit_discrepancies: Using independently converged final-mu weights instead of glm's saved IRLS working quantities gave covariance differences below 2e-7. Reconstructing the documented saved-IRLS convention reproduced covariance below 7e-15. This is a numerical iteration convention, not a production error.

An initial exact R identical() attribute check was false for freshly reconstructed cluster/strata tables. Numeric all.equal(), observation IDs, weights and design df agree. The original 53-check CSV is preserved; R2_verified_checks.csv transparently resolves the attribute-only check and adds three follow-up checks. The currently saved audit_core.R uses the corrected numerical equality check.

visual_review.result: Readable forest labels and t-based OR intervals; mosaic and Pearson residual exploration labelled as unweighted. Standardized mosaic residual and Pearson residual panel are different declared diagnostics.

reporting_notes: Primary n=21458 differs from the published n=21800. Present as partial reproduction under fixed declared eligibility, without claiming an exact reproduction or modifying definitions to match.
Naive Welch t has the No-minus-Yes sign while survey t is Yes-minus-No. Two-sided p values are unaffected. State contrast direction when interpreting signed statistics.
Rao-Scott F is the complex-survey inferential result. Ordinary Pearson, Yates and Fisher remain educational comparisons; mosaic residuals are descriptive SRS diagnostics.

Medication skip logic uses binary-code NA under known negative branches. The separate raw-data reviewer reported two raw BPQ050A refusal/dont-know responses overall and one in the R2 domain; zero were classified as medication_structural_no overall or in the domain. This does not affect current results. Restricting structural skips to raw NA would make the future implementation robust to contradictory responses.

The production core handler records pipeline warnings; an empty warnings log does not cover R process startup locale warnings. Independent scripts emitted locale startup warnings and then set a supported UTF-8 locale.
Cross-sectional adjusted odds ratios describe association; do not label them risks, prevalence ratios or causal effects.

exposure_record.prior: Official Springer Methods/footnote responses also displayed published counts and estimates during plan review. The V extension explicitly includes published counts.
exposure_record.current: Core executed code, derived master, tables and saved model fits were read for numerical auditing.
exposure_record.tuning: None. Independent checks use fixed plan definitions and mathematical identities.

limitations: The audit checks derived-domain calculations and numerical inference, not source XPT extraction or every manifest row, which are assigned to the data reviewer.
This acceptance does not cover Model 2/3, age/smoking interactions or supplemental model results. Extension audits are separate.
This acceptance is not an assertion that the original authors used the same eligibility, smoking variable or missing-value definitions.
